in writing. - 40% of cameroon is still covered by forest. because cameroon is the largest exporter of tropical timber in africa, and no other country is deforesting so heavily. experts estimate that in 10 to 15 years, the most ecologically valuable tree species in the congo basin will be gone if deforestation continues as it has been aimed at maximum yield. this ultimately threatens africa's green lungs, which are critical to global climate, and endangers cameroon's unique flora and fauna. the following are essential to protect cameroon's tropical forests: fighting corruption and bribery (both at the civil service level and among community owners of state forests), effective law enforcement, sustainable forestry, where only as much is cut as is grown, and better training of woodworkers to avoid damage to the forest floor during logging. european companies in particular are to be blamed, since some 80 per cent of the proceeds are shipped to europe. the eu must take the lead here and intervene directly! i therefore voted in favour of the present report because it is moving in the right direction.
in writing. − only if it is ensured that foreign firms no longer pimp out domestic firms that lack forestry and environmental know-how and if the congo gets its corruption under control does such an agreement make sense. the aim must be responsible and intergenerational forestry. until this awareness is ingrained in the minds of the local population, the practice of eye-wiping will continue. and as long as there are no significant penalties and sanctions for non-compliance with deforestation regulations, the eu agreement remains a paper tiger. even if only 'selective' deforestation is carried out, it should not be overlooked that many trees have to be removed during transportation itself, for example for the construction of transport roads. the agreement is not a miracle, but it is a step in the right direction and that is why i voted for it.

early stages of clinical development. a crucial point to emphasise is the fact that we do not have clinical data to support the idea that any of the candidate vaccines currently in development could demonstrate better efficacy than the vaccine that is currently in use, i.e. the bacillus calmette-guérin vaccine. to reach the market, new candidate vaccines must be able to increase efficacy over bacillus calmette-guérin or be able to replace it as a better vaccine. the fact is that we still do not have this important data today. the tbvi initiative should not be considered in isolation from other initiatives to support clinical trials. in order to address bottlenecks in clinical development, the european and developing countries clinical trials partnership, or edctp, was set up as the partnerships, including the one presented by the tbvi initiative. the tbvi initiative has proposed a model which has the potential to become a useful tool in the future. but this requires a thorough in writing. - i welcome today's decision on consumer law. we have taken an important decision for europe's citizens, businesses and the single market. it is gratifying that it has been possible to find a reasonable approach to partial unification of the multitude of european legal systems. nevertheless, from the austrian point of view, there are some problematic points which must now be urgently addressed and clarified in the trilogue negotiations between parliament, the council and the commission: (1) the so-called 'track element' must be included in the text. the 'start-up' element means that if you call a beautician at home to use her services (i.e. you start the business relationship yourself), for example, you can no longer have a right of withdrawal. (2) ensure that there is no additional burden on smes, provided that sufficient consumer protection is ensured. finally, the additional financial and administrative burden on smes would be passed on to the customer. the the commission has also proposed that chapter iv and chapter v (guarantee and abusive clauses) be deleted, since, despite lengthy negotiations, it has not been possible to achieve the full harmonisation sought. the deletion would avoid a stalemate and open up new possibilities in the trilogue negotiations. the the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the protection of consumers in respect of the use of electronic communications networks.
in writing. - i voted for the compromise package on consumer rights negotiated between the political groups because it allowed some improvements to be made to the commission's proposal for a directive. it is important that the basis of the directive is again minimum harmonisation and services such as those in the health or social field have been excluded from the directive. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of consumers in respect of the sale of consumer goods. also, purchases at trade fairs are now qualified as doorstep sales, whereas in austria, until now, purchases at trade fairs were treated legally as purchases in a shop. the commission has not yet adopted a proposal for a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the priority here is chapter v of the directive, with which the s&d group is absolutely dissatisfied. we want to avoid making the list of abusive contractual clauses exhaustive, and to allow member states to extend it without restriction, according to their level of consumer protection. many consumers in member states with a long tradition of consumer protection would otherwise experience deterioration. i therefore voted in favour of referring the matter back to committee so that these essential points can also be resolved and improved.
in writing. − the european network and information security agency (enisa) was established in 2004. its task is to ensure network and information security within the eu. it is also responsible for developing a culture of network and information security for citizens, consumers, businesses and public sector organisations in the european union. the aim of exercises such as the recent one on cybercrime is to ensure security in case of emergency. the commission has already made a number of proposals to this effect, and i am sure that the commission will be able to accept them. i did not vote for the report because i fear that the citizens will have to bear the additional costs without any tangible benefits.
in writing. − despite the financial crisis, the eu has been and is continually building up additional authorities, with a new agency being created for each issue and problem. between 2005 and 2009, the budget for eu agencies more than doubled, and the number of staff increased by 65%. the added value is more than questionable: the results are not good and the controls are inadequate. the average annual cost to taxpayers of eu agencies is €579 million. i am clearly against the opening of new agencies; the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. i have therefore voted against the report on the creation of a new information security agency. the commission has more than enough trained officials to take on this task.
in writing. − in 2004, the european network and information security agency was established for a period of five years. its 57 employees are involved in developing network and information security for citizens and consumers, businesses and eu public sector organisations. their tasks included both risk analysis and prevention. the continuous and ever-accelerating development of information and communication technologies and their essential importance for society and the economy will also determine the need for this agency in the future. but i have been calling for a business review of the eu agencies for some time, there are already initiatives to review the whole system, and until such a review is completed i will not agree to renew this agency.

in writing. − goods and technology for civilian and possible military purposes should be subject to equal conditions of competition in all member states. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the safety of the products is not compromised. the aim is to counteract an artificial reduction in the selling prices of european exports - a clear strengthening of european smes. i voted in favour of the amended proposal for a regulation because transparency and security must be the first priority for such goods and technologies.
in writing. − exports of dual-use goods and technology are tightly regulated within the eu. the term covers in particular goods and technology which can also serve a military purpose. in order to prevent abuse in the export industry, there are four types of export authorization: the community general export authorization, national export authorizations, worldwide export authorizations and individual export authorizations. each one is valid within the eu. there are also international export control regimes to which the eu is committed and where the commission is trying to improve the eu's standing. these include the australia group, of which the commission is a full member and in which each of the 27 states, as well as the usa, canada, japan, south korea and australia, participate; the nuclear suppliers group, in which the commission has observer status and the eu-27 with the usa and russia participate; the wassenaar arrangement, in which the commission has no status but all eu member states except cyprus are full members; and the background technology control regime, in which the commission also has no status and only 19 member states are full members. in order not to infringe the principle of subsidiarity, i voted accordingly.
in writing. − public or publicly supported export credit agencies are important financiers of public financing of private sector projects, including in developing countries. they are still gaining in importance for european companies' investments in times of tight budgets, provided they do not have to refinance themselves with taxpayers' money. as the risk assessment of public export credit agencies is completely different from that of private bank lending, there can be distortions of competition in international trade, as the example of china illustrates. for this reason, there are a number of regulations, such as oecd and wto agreements, which fix repayment periods and a minimum premium rate. the evaluation, in order to exclude misuse and to prevent refinancing from taxpayers' money, requires standards for greater transparency through the eu-wide obligation to disclose annual balance sheet reports, etc. it is questionable whether the proposed measures will achieve greater transparency. i abstained from the vote.

in writing. − in addition to pledging more than 415 million in emergency aid, the eu is also responding to the flood disaster in pakistan with special trade measures to boost pakistan's exports. the european commission proposed a package of 75 tariff lines covering pakistan's main export sectors in the areas most affected by the floods. pakistan's trade with the union is mainly in textiles and clothing products, which according to the commission represented 73,7% of pakistan's exports to the union in 2009. the eu considers that the granting of these trade preferences is likely to have only limited impact on the internal market and to have no negative impact on the least developed wto members. nevertheless, it is expected that the unilateral removal of the duties will lead to an infringement procedure of the world trade organisation. if pakistan is allowed to join the list of countries which enjoy special customs benefits, i.e. to be included in the so-called 'gsp plus' list, then that will be the end of it. uncoordinated rapid fire is of little use. the textile and clothing industry in particular is in crisis in a number of member states because of the transformation. the negative effects of trade preferences cannot therefore be excluded, which is why i rejected the report.

in writing. − since the lisbon treaty, the commission has the exclusive right to negotiate and conclude bilateral investment agreements with third countries. there are currently over 1000 agreements and some 200 are currently under negotiation, led by member states. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council adopt a common position on the proposal for a directive on the approximation of the laws of the member states relating to the labelling of foodstuffs for human consumption. the first reading of parliament gave a strong signal and called for a solid and secure phase of the transfer of legislation.
in writing. − what has failed at wto and oecd level, namely to shed light on the jungle of bilateral investment agreements, cannot be expected to succeed at eu level. at the higher level, an attempt was made to create comprehensive multinational regimes for fdi, i.e. foreign direct investment, applicable to all sectors of the economy. this will probably be more effective in the long run, but it will depend on the actual design. the problem is that binding bit arbitration awards based on international law may bind member states in a way that could lead to eu infringement proceedings in favour of an investor. there's still no solution for that. the report also failed to take into account potential negative aspects of investment policy, such as the fear of job losses and wage cuts by the local population due to outsourcing and relocation of production. and direct investment is far from the miracle cure it is being touted as. some developing countries have had to learn this the hard way. i have rejected this report for the reasons i have given.

in writing. − following the armed conflict with russia in 2008 and the impact of the global financial crisis, georgia is facing serious financial problems. already in january this year, the eu agreed a €46 million aid package for georgia, of which €23 million will be paid as a loan and another €23 million as a grant to the country. the €46 million is part of an eu financial assistance package of around €500 million agreed by the eu in october 2008. this second tranche of eu macro-financial assistance, the first of which was implemented in 2009-10, is designed to help georgia meet its external financing needs and is subject to strict conditionality. the first signs of success are already apparent in the fact that real gdp growth in 2010 was 6.3%, reflecting a recovery in economic activity. however, there are signs that the money is not being used efficiently enough. however, this is unacceptable in view of the budgetary situation in the vast majority of eu countries. i am in favour of financial support in principle, but i abstained from voting in the final vote.

in writing. −antibiotics are naturally produced metabolites of fungi or bacteria used to fight bacterial infections. they are given preventive feeding, among other things. resistance means that they have lost the ability to kill bacteria or inhibit their growth. to prevent this, it is advisable to follow the doctor' s instructions. however, resistant germs from animals can be transmitted to humans and pose a high health risk; in fact, it can lead to antibiotic resistance in humans. the report was therefore approved in order to finally encourage research into animal production without antimicrobials.

member of the commission. − mr president, as the rapporteur, jo leinen, said, the purpose of the commission proposal is indeed to establish a common legal framework for the collection, compilation, transmission and evaluation of european environmental economic accounts in order to facilitate more balanced decision-making with the goal of sustainable development. with the presentation of this proposal the commission has delivered its first item on the ‘beyond gdp’ road map. at a time when we are striving, in europe, to achieve a resource-efficient and sustainable economy, this data will allow us to link environmental factors to economic ones and thus offers the possibility of more comprehensive and better-informed policy making. following very fruitful cooperation between the three institutions, i believe we have reached our common objective, namely the establishment of this framework regulation on european environmental economic accounts with its first set of three modules, which cover air emissions accounts, environmentally-related taxes or levies and material flow accounts. currently this data is collected on a voluntary basis by the majority of member states. for the most part, therefore, the collection of the relevant data will not impose any additional burden on respondents, as the member states concerned should be able to compile the data by using existing data sources. with this regulation we have established an important basis for statistical information about the interplay between the economy and the environment, which we hope to expand with further modules in the future as included in the report and the draft resolution. as the various other possible modules are at different stages of methodological maturity, including for instance timber and fish as well as unused extraction, a modular structure has been adopted for the regulation with a view to possibly introducing new modules as annexes to the core text in the future. as agreed, the commission will report to parliament and the council every three years on the development of new modules and, if appropriate, the commission may also put forward new legislative proposals for the new modules. let me conclude by thanking the rapporteur, jo leinen, the shadow rapporteur, mr martin and all the members of the committee on the environment and the committee on economic and monetary affairs for their constructive approach and their very valuable contributions.

in writing. − the eu-canada agreement on civil aviation safety, which supplements the air transport agreement with canada, aims to remove technical barriers to trade. the main objective is to minimise as far as possible duplication of assessments, tests and checks and to ensure uniform certification. the commission will also be responsible for the implementation of the programme. the cooperation and mutual recognition of certifications should cover the areas of airworthiness and maintenance. the potential for the future lies in full mutual recognition. in addition to the joint committee, which is to deal with practical problems and prevent disputes, joint inspections, investigations and the exchange of safety data are also planned. it is to be welcomed that strict safeguards allow, where necessary, the suspension of the recognition of the findings of the other competent authority or the termination of the agreement in whole or in part. as long as product authorisation procedures are shorter and simpler without lowering safety standards, the agreement is to be welcomed.
in writing. − this recommendation deals with the agreement on civil aviation safety signed on behalf of the (then) european community on 6 may 2009. at present, only six member states have bilateral product certification agreements with canada. these will be repealed when the eu-canada agreement on civil aviation safety enters into force. the strict safeguards allow, if it is advisable, to suspend the recognition of the findings of the other competent authorities or to terminate the agreement. this may be done in full or in part. as long as product authorisation procedures are shorter and simpler without lowering safety standards, the agreement is to be welcomed.
in writing. − the agreement aims to minimise duplication of assessments, tests and checks by allowing both parties to use each other's certification system. this mutual trust in the parties' systems is based on convergence of requirements and regulatory processes, but also on regular consultations between the parties and the establishment of a joint committee. the shorter and cheaper product authorization procedures that this will enable will save millions of dollars annually for companies in this sector and will increase their competitiveness. the agreement makes the market more competitive but also safer, as it obliges the supervisory authorities to cooperate fully.
in writing. − the strategy report on the implementation of operational programmes co-financed under cohesion policy is a new instrument which will be essential for transparency and, in future, for the public's understanding of this complex issue. the court of auditors repeatedly notes enormous irregularities in the payment of subsidies. this instrument, if properly applied, could make a major contribution to stopping this. i therefore support the rapporteur's proposals for improvement, particularly those relating to the future quality of the reports drawn up by the member states, so that effective control is ensured in the future.

in writing. - awareness of food and especially its ingredients has changed considerably over the years. people are becoming more careful about what they eat, but the trend in the food sector is also clearly towards consuming products made at home. seasonal food is booming. it is precisely when diseases or pathogens reappear in the food sector, as recently in the case of ehec, that the population increasingly relies on local and familiar products. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft directive on the labelling of foodstuffs. ingredients should not be able to hide behind obscure abbreviations that either confuse or reassure the consumer. the same applies to the indication of the country of origin. for these reasons, the eu now wants to introduce a uniform eu-wide labelling requirement on food packaging. the information must be uniform throughout and be appropriate, formulated and legible in such a way as to ensure full transparency for the consumer. i believe that this is an important step towards ensuring that the population has a good diet and thus also towards a lasting improvement in public health. however, since the food industry is to bear the costs of the new labelling procedure, a price increase in the food sector is not excluded. i have taken this into account in my voting behaviour.

in writing. − under the current system, there is no truly uniform system in the european union for controlling the export and transport of dual-use goods such as nuclear materials and chemical and conventional weapons. decisions on these issues are taken in the eu's common foreign and security council behind closed doors without open debate, uniform criteria or the participation of the european parliament as eu legislator. not even all eu member states are represented in the organisations that manage the export of such dangerous goods. the baltic states, as well as cyprus, malta, slovakia, slovenia and romania, for example, are not members of the missile technology control regime. as a result, trade decisions by one eu member state can threaten the security interests of another, as we have already seen. this report supports amendments to european union legislation to establish a single eu system for the collection, dispatch and storage of export licences for dual-use goods and to impose on the commission an obligation to inform the european parliament of licences issued. on such fundamental issues as foreign and security policy, there must be a clear solidarity between eu member states. the amendments proposed in the report will introduce an improved, uniform and transparent system for regulating the export of arms, nuclear materials, missiles and similar technologies.
in writing. - dual-use goods are goods which are intended for civilian use but which, because of their characteristics, can be used for military purposes. a list of such goods has been drawn up under international export control regimes (annex i) and has been made subject to a special authorization requirement. the background to this community regulation now being put forward is to improve transparency and to increase responsibility for these types of goods and technologies. i therefore voted in favour of the proposal.

the rapporteur. - mr president, i have to say something. the title is too broad, but it hides a subject of enormous importance both for the institutions of the union and for the citizens. the focus of my report is on how european law is implemented and applied in the member states - the european law that we are developing and adopting here in this house with an enormous investment of time, resources and also commitment. if this right is not taken seriously in the member states, then this work - as the saying goes - has been for nothing. a parliament which does not take itself seriously and does not see that the rules it has laid down are applied would be leading itself into the absurd. the treaties, on the other hand, provide for a probative remedy, namely the commission as guardian of the treaties, which should monitor the process of application and implementation, up to the initiation of infringement actions, if agreement cannot be reached with the member state. this is the case, for example, with questions such as the recognition of professional qualifications, which can be very important for an individual's destiny, or with certain environmental issues, land ownership issues, or anything else that directly affects citizens. in most cases, the commission acts on the basis of a complaint by a complainant. these complainants, these citizens, are ultimately - and this is particularly important to me - our early warning system, which is designed to alert us to malfunctions in member states when we apply it and enable us to correct them here too. the role of the complainant is therefore central to the whole process. the citizens must have the actual opportunity to complain and then also be given information on how that complaint is being dealt with and whether there are consequences and, if not, why not. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the waste is disposed of in a way that is not harmful to the environment. my report also questions the practice in the so-called pilot project, where the commission, in the event of a citizen's complaint, unfortunately does not always fulfil its information obligations towards the complainant and prefers to negotiate with the member states behind the scenes. the citizen is then left in the rain as a complainant without information. this is not reasonable! that is why we have included a proposal in my report which proposes a at least partial codification of this process, with fixed deadlines and information obligations. this is clearly in line with the treaties and does not in any way restrict the commission, but helps it. in conclusion, in times of euroscepticism, it is more important than ever to respond to citizens' complaints and to ensure transparency in the handling of their complaints. i think we must all take this into account here.
mr president, mr commissioner, and mr president of the polish presidency! the creation of eu law is really anything but easy. on the contrary, it is extremely difficult for ordinary citizens to see through the intricate ways in which european law is being created, implemented and enforced. smart regulation, intelligent legislation, i see as a winning match between a good football team: the interaction between the institutions commission european parliament council must be harmonious, fast and orderly, that is to say, low-cost, but above all democratic. this means that the national parliaments, the eesc, the committee of the regions, civil society and - i stress this - the social partners must also be sufficiently involved. i would like to point out a shortcoming in the otherwise excellent karim report: i miss the mention of the social partners in this report. social dialogue is enshrined in eu primary law. the report merely states that all relevant stakeholders should be consulted. this does not take sufficient account of the specific nature of trade unions, but also of employers' representations. finally, the social partners themselves can be legislators at eu level, for example through social partners' agreements. the second point to be made is that smart regulation must not be used to water down the eu's minimum standards, particularly those on the protection of workers, in order to reduce standards that are only temporary.
i would like to thank the commissioner for his reply. the principle of subsidiarity is enshrined in the lisbon treaty, but it remains purely theoretical. just to give you a few examples: under the flexibility clause in article 352 of the treaty on the functioning of the european union, the eu may adopt rules without the consent of national parliaments if this is necessary to achieve the objectives of the treaties. listen to this! the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them. in the so-called passerelle clause, article 311, the eu gives itself the possibility and the right to levy its own taxes. what about subsidiarity? the only way to achieve better legislation is to have it in the institutions directly elected by the people, namely the european parliament and, of course, especially the national parliaments.

in writing. − although progress has been made in recent years in europe in road safety, the target of halving the number of road deaths per year has not been met. a number of measures are being taken to achieve the objective. however, these remain rather vague and it is doubtful whether they will reduce the number of road deaths to the desired extent. it is also important to obtain more comparable data on the causes of injuries and accidents in order to achieve the desired level of coordination between member states. we should also be aware of the role of lorries in serious road accidents, which are becoming more dangerous in the face of increasingly competitive pressures, and of the fact that scrap vehicles are still on the roads of europe. of course, it would be desirable if the population regularly attended first aid courses. but such a visit cannot be imposed on road users. that is why i voted no.
in writing. the majority of the european road network is designed to be of the truck size typical today. however, the commission is in favour of the so-called 'gigaliners'. gigaliner are up to 25 metres long and weigh up to 60 tonnes. these giants obscure the view of motorists, and overtaking distances on long-distance roads increase dramatically. furthermore, significantly higher damage is expected in both man and machine if a collision occurs. the eu's target of halving road fatalities by 2020 is therefore far from being achieved. care should be taken to ban these 'gigaliners' from road traffic. i have voted against the report because it does not deal with this danger.
in writing. − the measures proposed in the report, some of which have already been detailed, are comprehensible, proportionate and necessary. although the number of road deaths has been declining for years, there is still work to be done. i agreed to it.
in writing. - the report makes some reasonable points. i support the call for financial compensation for those who have to be relocated because of dam projects and welcome the reference to the need for impact assessments in the construction of dams. these can have a massive impact on the countries bordering them and cause considerable damage to the environment. i am not aware of any reference to the misappropriation of aid money allocated for the construction of dams. according to estimates by transparency international (tpi), 70 percent of the flood authority budget in pakistan has been misappropriated. we must go the other way and not continue with the old practice of helping. furthermore, the report contains inappropriate links with climate policy objectives which cannot be justified in the context of funding for dam reinforcement in developing countries. i have therefore decided to abstain.
in writing. the massive flooding disasters of recent years have claimed countless lives and caused billions in property damage. the report takes up the recommendations of the united nations and draws on the findings of the world commission on dams, which recommends implementing fewer new projects, optimising existing dams, tackling the root causes of problems rather than moderately successfully tackling the symptoms and further undermining the eu's millennium development goals, the achievement of which is already highly questionable. i agreed to the report.
in writing. − the continuing increase in global food insecurity poses new challenges to the mdgs and requires a review of eu strategies in development cooperation. a new communication on food safety was adopted by the eu commission in march 2010. the main points are: increasing the food supply by supporting small-scale food production, optimising food access and ensuring a balanced diet. once again, a report by the european parliament points to the volatility of prices and the serious effects of speculation in derivatives of essential food commodities. i agreed to it.
in writing. the motion for a resolution refers to the inclusion of unilateral declarations by member states in the minutes of council meetings. the european parliament's transition and over-riding are particularly worrisome. the measures called for in the resolution are simply unnecessary. the report rightly refers in its recitals to the court's assessment of the statements. it denies them any legal force. the commission has not yet taken a decision on the matter, but it is still in the process of being drawn up. i therefore believe that the member states can continue to include their statements in the minutes of the council meetings. i therefore voted against the motion for a resolution.
in writing. - in principle, acts should be self-explanatory. the interpretation is also usually based on the operative part or the recitals. parliament, as the only directly elected eu body, should be informed of unilateral declarations by member states at all stages of the legislative process. i am, however, opposed to the unilateral declarations of the member states being accepted as additional grounds for interpretation. the lawyer has the right to be informed of the contributions and concerns of the member states, even if these are only marginal. i also see no reason why these statements should not be published in the official journal of the european union. that is why i voted against this report.
in writing. − i support the report on a new trade policy under the europe 2020 strategy as it identifies important areas for a sustainable and competitive europe. the rapporteur has provided a balanced and concise approach to a review of the eu's trade strategy, which the commission should take to heart. the commitments to a multilateral trading system, the removal of trade barriers and the integration of sustainability chapters in bilateral trade agreements are a clear guideline.
in writing. − the eu has set out a number of strategies with a variety of objectives, which it has largely failed to achieve. in this context, it may be useful to first evaluate the old strategies and to find out why they were not achieved and why some strategies exist only on paper. at eu level, when we talk about strengthening global competitiveness, we often only refer to large companies and multinational groups. the motor of the economy and the main employer, however, is the large number of small and mediumsized enterprises, whose importance is always emphasized in the various strategies on paper, but which in practice have little access to subsidies and are burdened with ever-increasing bureaucracy. as the present report does not deal at all with the role of smes, i did not agree.
in writing. − in times of globalisation and emerging markets such as china, there is a greater need than ever to improve the eu's competitiveness and economic standing. in this context, there are a number of issues which are not adequately addressed in this report, although they are key elements of sustainable competitiveness in the eu: firstly, the interests and problems of smes, which form the backbone of our economy, are not being taken into account enough: i am thinking in particular of the access of smes to finance for international trade, to enable them to internationalise and thereby to promote their innovative capacity. this brings me to another point: european companies (and smes in particular) still have great difficulty in enforcing their intellectual property rights in third countries, especially in asia. we must urgently act against barriers to trade from third countries, both tariff and non-tariff. the eu imposes strict competition rules on itself, but at the same time we must also combat unfair state aid to domestic production in third countries. otherwise, our companies will soon be left behind. i have not voted for the report because these points have not been taken into account.
in writing. − the 2007 evaluation of the eu strategy for a globally competitive europe shows that many of the objectives set have not been achieved. the eu's share of global value added is declining, losing further to new entrants in the world market such as china or india. the 36 million jobs in the eu that depend on external trade require analyses and policies that respond to the needs of the union and its citizens.

in writing. − the report on the strengthening of fiscal surveillance and economic policy coordination addresses the need for coordination of member states' economic policies through stability and convergence programmes, continuous evaluation, complemented by strict monitoring measures and an effective enforcement mechanism, while strengthening national ownership. the aim is to ensure sustainable growth by coherently linking related policies and subjecting financial markets to increased regulation and supervision. the involvement of national parliaments and the european parliament throughout the coordination process ensures democratic legitimacy and transparency (the stability and convergence programmes are published). i agreed to it.
in writing. − together with the report on the implementation of the excessive deficit procedure, the report on budgetary surveillance adds several essential requirements to the legislative package on economic governance in the euro area. the stability and growth pact provides that the adjustment to and compliance with the medium-term budgetary objective can be ensured by the introduction of an interest-bearing deposit temporarily extended to euro area countries that have not achieved sufficient budgetary consolidation. as the case of greece shows, the falsification of financial statistics by one country can have disastrous consequences for the whole of the european union, and it is therefore vital to improve without delay both the collection of statistical data and the verification of the data submitted, as well as to introduce serious penalties for the member states responsible. the report on budgetary surveillance in the euro area provides for the establishment of precisely this type of sanction against member states, namely for falsifying statistical data or for submitting incorrect data as a result of serious negligence. the penalty would be up to 0,2% of national gdp. although sceptical about the requirement for the commission to prepare proposals for the creation of eurobonds, it nevertheless considers the adoption of the above requirements to be useful.
in writing. - i am in favour of a substantial strengthening of the stability and growth pact in the euro area. compliance with such obligations can only be achieved through the effective enforcement of severe penalties. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament and the council should be given the opportunity to present their opinions on the draft budget for the financial year 2000 and to present their opinions on the draft budget for the financial year 2000 in the form of a report to the european parliament and the council. the lessons of the stability and growth pact will be learned by punishing manipulation of statistics with fines of a certain magnitude.
in writing. − the current experience of economic and monetary union shows that the primary tasks of european countries, especially those in the euro area, include improving economic governance, putting in place an effective system to prevent excessive government deficits, and strengthening financial market regulation and surveillance. the european parliament's report provides for the introduction of a specific alert mechanism to detect risks of macroeconomic imbalances in the union in good time. the warning mechanism would be based on regular assessments of the financial and macroeconomic situation of the member states by the commission. this will include the development of a set of specific, indicative and transparent indicators, developed jointly by the european parliament, the council and the commission, covering both nominal and real convergence, as well as internal and external imbalances between countries, changes in productivity and its drivers, such as research and development, foreign/domestic investment, and changes in sectors, including energy, affecting gdp and the current account. the indicators should also be reviewed and updated at least annually in order to avoid a situation like that in ireland, where the approach of the crisis was not detected in time due to outdated indicators. if a member state is found to have macroeconomic imbalances, it would be advised to implement them within a set timeframe, involving stakeholders, including the social partners, where appropriate.
in writing. - the ten-year anniversary of economic and monetary union has already revealed increasing divergences between member states, which were already evident before the crisis. the correction system for these imbalances is intended to prevent europe from falling into the extreme situation that we have been in since 2008.
in writing. − an improved economic governance system in the eu must be based on mutually agreed policies for sustainable growth and employment, based on the core principles of the stability and growth pact. particular attention should be paid to the development of the internal market, the promotion of international trade and competitiveness, the effective regulation of national budgets, the prevention of macroeconomic fluctuations, and more effective supervision and regulation of financial markets. to achieve this, it is first necessary to adopt specific requirements for national budgets, together with sanctions for long-term non-compliance with these requirements. the report sets out the requirements for the member state to meet in the event of an inadequate budgetary system or a budget deficit in excess within a period of at least six months. in the event of a particularly critical situation, the member state may be required to take action within three months in order to reduce the budget deficit within a year. to ensure the necessary discipline among the euro area member states, it has been agreed to give the commission a stronger supervisory role, which will in future not only assess the economic situation in the member states but also undertake special monitoring missions to them, accompanied by the european central bank if necessary. penalties are also provided for a fine of up to 0,5% of the national gdp that would be paid into the budget of the european financial stability facility. these are all essential steps towards a coherent monetary policy, without which there can be no single currency union.
in writing. − the long-term sustainability of public finances is central to preventing a situation like the one we have today in the future. the decision that a member state is in an excessive deficit shall be taken by the council taking into account developments in the medium-term economic situation, including contributions from labour, capital formation and the productivity factor, developments in the medium-term budgetary position and developments in the medium-term government debt, and the dynamics and sustainability of the latter . the implementation of pension reforms will also be adequately taken into account in the assessment of compliance with the deficit and debt criterion in view of future challenges, which is a proactive measure. i agreed to the report.
in writing. − the eurozone crisis and the current difficulties are largely due not only to the lack of a single monetary policy but also to an inaccurate and easily falsifiable system of producing and compiling statistics. i would therefore like to support the report on the proposal for a council directive on the requirements for the budgetary authorities of the member states, which applies to all eu member states and which focuses specifically on the provision of sound public accounting practices and quality statistics, as well as on independent auditing of national budgetary matters, which are fundamental components of the eu's fiscal surveillance system and its effective functioning. the council has encouraged the member states, both for their own needs and in the interests of the european union, to draw up and make publicly available tables containing, as far as possible, precise data on the compliance of this directive and the transposition measures. based on the recommendations of the commission and the council, the report contains all the elements essential for the overall transparency and evaluation of the financial and budgetary structures of government, which will be reflected in the commission's annual evaluations and progress reports.
in writing. − the experience and lessons learned from the crisis should be used to adapt and improve the provisions of the stability and growth pact and to make the necessary additions to the provisions on national fiscal frameworks. the directive on the requirements for the budgetary frameworks of the member states contains provisions on the transparency of budgetary data and on the planning and monitoring of medium-term objectives. i agreed to it.
in writing. - i voted against the reports by mr wortmann-kool (a7-0178/2011), mr goulard (a7-0180/2011), mr feio (a7-0179/2011) and mr ford (a7-0184/2011), as they do not represent a balanced package of economic governance. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the budgetary discipline is maintained, and that the budgetary authority is able to take action to ensure that the budgetary discipline is maintained. the package is socially unbalanced. it is yielding to the pressure of the financial markets and leaving the costs of the crisis to the citizens. there is a lack of democratic control over the most important economic policy decisions. in months of negotiations, our group has pushed for a compromise, but the conservative majority in the council and parliament has refused to budge a finger from its rigid austerity policy, even as it became increasingly clear that this approach was continually pushing europe further towards a 'double dip recession'. the s&d group has identified a clear alternative the exact wording can be found in the paper a just way out of the crisis (http://www.socialistsanddemocrats.eu/gpes/media3/documents/3574_de_fair_way_out_crisis_de_100908.pdf).
in writing. - the tightening of the stability pact is countering the worst of the ills by 'automating' the deficit procedures. the council has not yet taken a decision on the matter. however, this reform has not solved the current debt crisis in greece and portugal. both countries are unable to operate them and are therefore insolvent. the stability pact will not prevent a transfer union in the future. in the case of asymmetric shocks, the necessary exchange rate variance is the only criterion to be used for the formation of a monetary union. otherwise, a fiscal transfer union will be necessary. the only way to prevent a transfer union without democratic legitimacy is to split the monetary area into a hard and soft currency union. the effects of political wishful thinking and daydreaming in these centralistic measures can be studied in the context of the unrest in the southern member states. the european commission's reference to the observation of 'imbalances' is ineffective. in the worst case, competitiveness is penalized by 'too high' current account surpluses. in the positive scenarios, proposals to moderate wage increases resulting from incentive distortions in a misconstrued monetary area will be blown up. the political freedoms of the member states must under no circumstances be called into question. i therefore voted against this report and the other reports of the so-called six-pack which are related to it.

in writing. − the european globalisation adjustment fund, now extended in 2009, is designed to support workers who have lost their jobs through no fault of their own as a result of the economic and financial crisis. the 2009 amendment also changed two of the criteria: the requirement of a certain number of redundancies was reduced from 1000 to 500 and the co-financing rate was increased from 50% to 65%. this amendment renews an unconditional renewal without addressing any substantive issues or shortcomings. i therefore did not agree.

in writing. first of all, i would like to thank the rapporteur very much for having negotiated good compromises, despite massive opposition and many amendments, to produce this important report with effective measures to combat poverty and social exclusion. many eu citizens are acutely poor or at risk of poverty, and the crisis is exacerbating this deplorable situation. in austria alone, 12% of the population is at risk of poverty - half of them are manifestly poor. in most member states, where the social welfare system is not as developed, the situation is even more dramatic. it is our responsibility to provide these people with a way out. the commission has therefore proposed that the council adopt a new regulation on the protection of the environment. the most important is to strengthen the welfare state and ensure that public services are of high quality and accessible to all. but it is not enough to combat the effects of poverty. the first is to find concrete strategies to prevent poverty. the report recognises the special needs of the most vulnerable groups: by recognising that the priority of tackling child poverty is prevention, this report makes an important contribution to long-term sustainable development in order to achieve one of the key objectives of the europe 2020 strategy - to reduce by 20 million by 2020 the number of people at risk of poverty.
although the european union is one of the richest regions in the world, it is a matter of grave concern that more than 80 million people in the union are at least at risk of poverty. the fact that 20 million of them are children is particularly worrying. 2010 was the 'european year for combating poverty and social exclusion'. the theme was chosen to reaffirm and further advance the eu's objective of reducing poverty. real progress in this area can only be achieved if there is a will to act together with mutually supportive and complementary measures at all levels .

in writing. - in the proposal for a directive on the coordination of safeguards which, for the purposes of the formation of a public limited liability company, are required by member states of companies incorporated under public law and of companies whose capital is maintained or altered, the european parliament proposed two amendments concerning the revision of the minimum capital required for the formation of a public limited liability company. i agreed to it.
in writing. the 1974 convention deals primarily with questions of safety and liability which may arise in the carriage of passengers and their baggage by sea. the convention was revised by the protocol adopted in 2002 in order to regulate more efficiently the areas of liability in the event of the fault or negligence of the carrier, compulsory insurance for the transported persons and the right to assert claims arising directly with the insurer. the member states retain the right to regulate independently all aspects not covered by the protocol. in addition, higher liability limits may be established. since articles 10 and 11 of the protocol cover matters relating to the areas of judicial cooperation in civil matters within the meaning of article 81 tfeu, those provisions will be dealt with in a separate act. there is no doubt that accession to the protocol will create a general legal framework which will harmonise the rights of persons carried on maritime transport in a positive way and thus represent an improvement on the current situation. however, some of the provisions are unclear, which is why i abstained.
in writing. the athens convention on the carriage of passengers and their luggage by sea of 1974 dealt mainly with the safety of passenger ships and various passenger rights. however, the nature and extent of the liability of carriers and the minimum insurance requirements were not sufficiently regulated in the 1974 convention and the 2002 convention was amended by a protocol accordingly. in 2005, the european commission proposed a further amendment to the protocol, which further standardised the liability of carriers in the event of accidents (updated in 2010). the eu hereby becomes a party to the athens convention. i agreed to it.
in writing. − articles 10 and 11 of the athens convention govern jurisdiction in civil and commercial matters and the recognition and enforcement of judgments in a member state. i agreed to it.
in writing. − the euro-mediterranean air transport agreement will replace the existing bilateral agreements that individual eu member states have concluded with jordan in this field. the aim is to create a level playing field for airlines in the 27 member states. the commission notes that the jordanian authorities have not provided any evidence that the services provided by the airlines in question are in fact provided by jordanian airlines. the main objectives of the agreement are to gradually open the market in terms of route access and capacity, to eliminate discrimination and distortions of competition, and to align jordanian aviation legislation with eu legislation in areas such as aviation safety, security and air traffic management. the agreement is the next step in the development of the 2002 association agreement, which has as its stated objective the creation of a free trade area between the eu and jordan. for the reasons described above, a common aviation area is expected to bring significant competitive advantages for the european airlines involved and a substantial improvement in travel conditions for end-users. i therefore voted in favour of concluding the agreement.
in writing. − the bilateral air services agreements between individual member states and third countries are brought together in an agreement where the eu replaces the third countries as contractual partners with the individual member states. the aim is to gradually open up the market to reciprocity in terms of route access and capacity, and to ensure compliance with eu legislation, in particular with regard to safety rules, including in jordanian aviation law. the consumer benefit is estimated by external studies at eur 30 million. the aim is also to establish a common euro-mediterranean airspace. i agreed to the deal.
in writing. − the mutual market opening will allow for non-discriminatory participation in the aviation space, and in future all air carriers will be able to offer their services in the eu and in georgia. the consumer benefit is estimated by external studies at around eur 17 million. i agreed to it.
in writing. the economic situation in the autonomous community of the canary islands is severely affected by a long-term downturn. the canary islands and the european union hope that the temporary suspension of the autonomous common customs tariff duties on imports into the canary islands will strengthen the competitiveness of local operators and thus stabilise the employment situation. end-use controls are intended to ensure that the goods imported duty-free are actually used by local enterprises on the islands and that there is no competitive consumption. the canary islands must also be able to use raw materials, parts and components intended for industrial processing and maintenance. it is to be feared that the dismal economic situation in the canary islands will be difficult to overcome without the help of the european union. the commission has already taken a number of measures to ensure that the canary islands are able to comply with the community's economic recovery programme. the measure will also have an impact on the european union's revenue, the extent of which is yet to be estimated. i have therefore abstained.
in writing. the proposal is to suspend temporarily the common customs tariff for the canary islands on the import of certain industrial products. the aim is to strengthen the competitiveness of regional economic operators and thus improve the employment situation in europe's peripheral regions, as already envisaged in the european economic recovery programme. in order to avoid distortion of competition, the duty-free goods should be subject to end-use controls, i.e. verification that they are actually used by canarian companies. i agreed to it.
in writing. − the iter nuclear research reactor management already indicated in 2009 that the costs of the iter reactor could increase by up to 100 per cent. the euratom research funds originally earmarked for this purpose in the eu's seventh framework research programme would not have been sufficient for the iter nuclear research reactor. the cost of building iter is estimated at eur 6.6 billion. according to these estimates, the contribution from the euratom budget would be around eur 5,3 billion, with france contributing around eur 1,3 billion. therefore, the euratom budget should be increased from the current eur 2,15 billion to around eur 5,3 billion, i.e. by around eur 3,15 billion, to make up the difference. the extent to which cooperation with the international energy agency (iaea) should be extended is highly questionable in view of its proposals for fukushima, such as lowering radiation levels. nor are there any 'future' nuclear power plants. i therefore reject this report in the strongest possible terms.
in writing. − for the 2012-13 european atomic energy community work programme, criteria are provided for evaluating proposals for indirect actions and selecting projects. the commission will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the member states and will continue to monitor the implementation of the acquis in the union. the safety, performance, resource efficiency and the objectives of the medical and industrial applications of radiation are dealt with in this proposal, as are the safety of nuclear installations and the disposal of radioactive waste. i am opposed to nuclear energy as such and since this proposal refers specifically to the iter project and highlights its new european dimension, i have rejected the report.

in writing. − for decades, a massive demographic shift has been taking place, with far-reaching consequences for the social fabric and massive economic impacts. the trend towards social integration is not yet as strong in the new eastern eu member states as in the old eu countries. the demographic change will certainly change the political, social, societal and economic situation in europe in a decisive way. the orphaning of entire areas of the countryside shows what will happen to rural areas in the future if the emigration of young people cannot be stopped. by now, it should be clear from initial studies of the costs and benefits of immigration that mass migration cannot be the answer to demographic change. the massive cuts to rural infrastructure, for example in the name of postal and rail liberalization, and school closures are further accelerating this emigration trend. as long as basic infrastructure conditions are not met, structural aid cannot reverse the trend. i cannot therefore agree with the report.

in writing. − by adopting the regulation on short selling and certain aspects of credit default swaps, the european union is seeking to harmonise the restrictions on short selling that have been imposed individually by the member states. credit default swaps are insurance against the default of loans and government bonds. however, you can now buy these insurance papers without being a creditor or a holder of government bonds. in this case, it is even advantageous if a company or a state cannot meet its payment obligations. finally, in this case the sum insured is paid to the holder of the credit default swaps. it is clear that these two financial instruments can contribute to increased instability in the markets, especially in times of financial and economic crisis, and therefore need to be subject to restrictions. the commission has also proposed that the european parliament should be consulted on the draft regulation on the protection of the financial interests of the union. i have therefore given my consent.
in writing. − short selling can intensify the downward spiral of stock prices, especially in financial instruments, in times of considerable financial instability. this creates systemic risks, jeopardises the viability of financial institutions. there is no specific eu legal framework for dealing with short selling issues, so the measures taken by member states during the financial crisis varied widely. in order to improve the functioning of european financial markets and to ensure a high level of consumer and investor protection, a common legal framework should be established for the rules and powers relating to short selling and credit default swaps and a higher level of coordination and coherence between member states should be ensured with regard to exceptional situations requiring action. in addition, it is appropriate to choose the form of a regulation, as some provisions directly require private operators to report and disclose net short positions and uncovered short sales in certain instruments. i therefore voted in favour of the report.
in writing. - i voted for the canfin report because, after lengthy negotiations with the council, the european parliament has succeeded in reaching an agreement and in achieving improvements in the sense of stricter regulation of short selling and credit default swaps. the eu parliament was able to convince the council of its position on many points in the trilogue negotiations. the trade in uncovered credit default swaps on sovereign debt, which have also boosted the sovereign debt of greece, portugal and spain and, more recently, italy, is severely restricted and only allowed with the approval of the european securities and markets authority. i have long been puzzled as to why the council has hesitated so long in the negotiations on this subject. at the beginning of the negotiations the council advocated a minimum, unambitious regulation of short selling. the negotiating skills of the eu parliament delegation in the trilogue negotiations are a major step forward in the fight against risky speculation. i also welcome the fact that this regulation will enter into force quickly, as a result of the agreement reached at first reading, and not be negotiated for another year or two. action is needed - and it must be swift and effective!
in writing. the proposed regulation provides a comprehensive framework for credit default derivatives. short selling of securities is attributed a not insignificant contribution to the current financial situation. clear guidelines on cooperation between esma and national authorities, backed up by a comprehensive transparency regime, including the restriction of uncovered short selling, are needed, starting from the broadest possible scope.

in writing. − the eu commission wants to publish a consumer policy agenda by may 2012 that goes beyond the scope of the 2007-2012 consumer strategy. this is to take account of the principle of the eu treaty that consumer interests must be taken into account in all relevant eu policies. the main focus is on the following areas: food, health and product safety; creating inclusive growth; reducing co2 emissions from local and regional food production; reducing inequalities among eu citizens (many cannot afford rent or a warm home); solidarity-based funding of social services accessible to all. in addition, the rights and interests of digital consumers must now also be taken into account in the legislation. i agreed to it.
in writing. - the number of online gambling sites is growing steadily. currently, around 10% of all games of chance (lottery games, sports betting, poker and bingo games) with a market volume of more than eur 10 billion in europe are played online, by telephone or via interactive television platforms. the legal situation varies widely within the eu member states, due to the principle of subsidiarity. while some countries have reservations about authorization, others have total bans and still others have a completely open and liberalized market. the lack of borders on the internet allows gambling operators from member states with open markets to be reached in countries where online gambling is prohibited. the commission has also proposed that the council should adopt a directive on the protection of workers from the risks related to exposure to asbestos. the commission is also proposing to extend the scope of the directive to cover the whole of the eu, including the european union, and to extend it to cover the whole of the eu. the commission has also proposed that the council should be able to adopt a decision on the matter. however, when it is proposed to dismantle the black market by creating a legal online gambling service, the principle of subsidiarity is de facto undermined. i therefore abstained.
in writing. - i voted for the report on online gambling because i believe it is important to prevent illegal online gambling. the provisions on the protection of minors and common consumer standards in online gambling are also highly desirable. the report takes account of the fact that the principle of subsidiarity must be respected. i am not in favour of harmonizing online gambling, but i am concerned that there can still be national restrictions because of the specific nature of gambling. the report calls on the commission to create uniform quality standards for national licensing models - which i think is desirable. austria is already setting high standards of consumer protection and is a good example of good practice.

in writing. − the so-called services of general interest are those services which the state considers to be of particular importance to the population and which, without state intervention and subsidies, could not be provided to all citizens in sufficient quantity. these include the running of hospitals, education, social housing and energy. the commission notes that the commission has not provided any evidence that the compensation granted by the state to the airlines in question was in fact granted to them in the form of state aid. the commission assesses whether state aid meets these requirements on the basis of the four altmark criteria. it is clear that services in the areas just described are far too important for prosperity and social peace in the individual eu countries for the european commission to decide whether aid is efficient and cost-effective. it should be left to the member states to assess the subsidies they grant on the basis of their needs. i therefore voted against the motion.
in writing. − services of general interest are services which are considered by the state or public authorities to be necessary for all citizens, but which can only be provided adequately by state intervention, in other words: ensuring universal access to these services and high quality at affordable prices. in 2005, the commission set out the prohibition and control of state aid in the dawi community framework: the legal instruments need to be more clearly defined and the administrative burden reduced. i agreed to it.

in writing. − the european union's cultural heritage seal aims to increase the sense of belonging of european citizens to the union through common elements to raise awareness among young people in particular. the award of the cultural seal is based on criteria precisely defined by the commission. a jury of experts (12 members appointed by the commission, the council and the european parliament) examines the sites proposed by each member state in a pre-selection procedure (two per year, of which a maximum of one is accepted). member states undertake to maintain the sites in accordance with criteria defined by the commission. if these criteria are met, which are assessed by the jury, the seal is awarded indefinitely; if not, it is revoked after two warnings and a period of 36 months. transnational sites are given priority for selection, and sites already awarded the seal are reassessed. the report has my vote because the amendments pay much more attention to the added value of the seal compared to other initiatives in the field of cultural heritage and also to ensure that only the most outstanding sites are really certified.
in writing. − in march 2010, the commission presented a proposal for a decision on the european heritage label, which extends an intergovernmental initiative launched in 2006. the overall objective of the proposal is to strengthen the sense of belonging of european citizens and their sense of belonging to the eu by highlighting the common elements of history and cultural heritage and promoting intercultural dialogue.

in writing. - in theory, research may have brought about greater nuclear safety. but safe nuclear power plants on paper are not reality. in this context, it should also be examined to what extent the suspicion that nuclear power plant operators outsource maintenance and safety checks and exert massive pressure on the staff to cover up defects has been reinforced. i am against this highly risky technology. instead of spending billions on this and thus artificially keeping it alive despite all the safety risks and the concerns about its profitability, the money spent on this should be better spent on developing alternative and future-oriented forms of energy. i have voted against the report on this point.
in writing. − in march 2011, the european commission presented a package of legislative proposals on nuclear research and training (20122013). the legislative package is intended to provide further support for nuclear research and development activities already carried out under the 7th european framework programme 2007-2011. in this vote i voted for a reform of the euratom treaty to strengthen the rights of information and to establish democratic control by the european parliament. i also voted for the amendment calling for nuclear disarmament. i rejected the report as such because of the additional funding for projects such as iter and the r & d programme, including the jet facility at culham research centre in the uk.
in writing. − given that the eu and the us together account for 50% of the world economy, a coordinated approach is needed, particularly in order to resolve the current economic crisis. the interconnectedness of our economies means that closer economic cooperation is the only way to restore stability and ensure prosperity in both regions. i therefore support the resolution's intention to develop a joint transatlantic initiative for growth and employment. i am critical of the proposed agreement on passenger data records between the eu and the usa. before taking further steps in this direction, it is necessary to ensure that the protection of personal data of european citizens is such that future misuse can be excluded beyond doubt. the commission has already made a number of proposals to the council, and i am sure that the council will be able to accept them.

in writing. − the open nature of the internet is a key element for competitiveness, economic growth, social development and the development of new innovations. it also provides for the free exchange of views and access to new knowledge. the exchange of information is being greatly accelerated by global networking. the internet is therefore of great importance to the world economy. in addition, more and more jobs can be created through the internet. the full potential of the internet requires a well-functioning internal market. i abstained because i believe that end-users still have too little control over their shared content and are too dependent on providers.
in writing. − net neutrality is not yet a topic of discussion among the general public, but this will change rapidly in the coming years, in line with society's increasing dependence on internet services. it is therefore appropriate to establish a common framework as a preventive measure to safeguard this freedom of information, consumer interests and pluralism for the future and to prevent anti-competitive behaviour. the resolution calls on the commission to ensure the consistent enforcement of the existing legal framework and to build on the net neutrality of eu internet governance. i agreed to it.
in writing. − at the initiative of norway, 46 states adopted the oslo declaration in february 2007, with the aim of achieving a global ban on cluster munitions by the end of 2008. as of 1 august 2010, the convention on cluster munitions (ccm) is in force, having been ratified by 38 states, with another 70 states in the process of ratification. the ccm prohibits the use of cluster munitions and their trade and calls on states to destroy the stock of cluster munitions. many of the major producers of these weapons have not yet signed the treaty, including brazil, india, pakistan, china, russia, and the united states. cluster bombs are a threat to civilians in particular, since unexploded submunitions are often found and detonated by innocent people. i voted for this resolution because i believe that every loophole, however small, which allows for the trade and storage or even the use of these lethal munitions must be closed.
in writing. − the eu has long been actively involved in mine clearance in third countries, which hampers post-conflict reconstruction. in the case of children who are injured mainly by explosive remnants of war, appropriate care is provided in appropriate education programmes. the resolution again stresses the serious dangers posed by cluster munitions and is firmly committed to further support for and implementation of the convention on the prohibition of anti-personnel mines. i agreed to it.
